item.description: Spiking Neural Networks Spiking neural networks are neural networks that communicate with discrete events called spikes instead of continuously passing around activation values at every step.

item.title: 2.1 How SNNs Learn
item.description: How SNNs Learn Now that a spike event can be treated as a prediction signal, learning becomes a concrete problem: a network receives input spikes, produces output spikes, compares that output with what should have happened, and changes its connections so the next response is better.

item.title: 2.2 Surrogate Gradient Training
item.description: You already know that a spiking neural network sends information as events: a neuron stays quiet while its input is too weak, then emits a spike when its internal signal crosses a threshold.
